citeAs: Rajpurkar, P., Zhang, J., Lopyrev, K., and Liang, P. (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv.
creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang (Stanford University)
description: SQuAD is a reading comprehension dataset of 100,000+ crowdworker-written questions on Wikipedia articles, where each answer is a text span from the corresponding passage. The paper reports 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 English Wikipedia articles.
name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question has 1 original answer, and questions in the development and test sets have at least 2 additional answers.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports human performance using inter-annotator agreement on development and test questions with at least three answers per question; human performance on the test set is 77.0% exact match and 86.8% F1.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions for each paragraph. Questions were entered in a text field and answers were highlighted in the paragraph; workers were given a sample paragraph and examples of good and bad questions and answers, were encouraged to use their own words, and copy-paste on the paragraph text was disabled. For development and test sets, additional workers selected the shortest answer span for each question and could leave a question unanswered if no span answered it.
rai:dataBiases: The collection interface encouraged workers to ask questions in their own words rather than copying phrases from the paragraph, reinforced by reminder prompts and disabling copy-paste, to reduce lexical overlap bias between questions and passages.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating passages from English Wikipedia, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages, and collecting additional answers for development and test questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data were English Wikipedia articles. The authors used Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10,000 articles of English Wikipedia, sampled 536 articles uniformly at random, and extracted individual paragraphs from them.
rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that answers are constrained to spans in the passage, making questions more constrained than more interpretative questions in advanced standardized tests. It also notes that 2.6% of development and test questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker and that some examples are ambiguous or do not have a unique answer.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From sampled Wikipedia articles, the authors extracted individual paragraphs, stripped away images, figures, and tables, discarded paragraphs shorter than 500 characters, and randomly partitioned articles into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for machine reading comprehension and question answering research, and is presented as a challenge problem for training and evaluating data-intensive models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses, POS tags, dependency parses, and NER tags for automatic analysis of answer types and syntactic divergence.
